tests.name: Quick Check
tests.description: Timed check on Dance Appreciation Skills

questions.question: Q: What does AO4 assess in GCSE Dance?
questions.correctAnswer: AO4 assesses the ability to analyse and evaluate dance, including professional works and own choreographic practice.

questions.question: Q: Explain the difference between describing and analysing a dance.
questions.correctAnswer: Describing means stating what you see (e.g. 'the dancers move in unison'); analysing means explaining how and why it works (e.g. 'unison creates a sense of unity reinforcing the choreographic intent').

questions.question: Q: Why must evaluation be supported by evidence?
questions.correctAnswer: Without evidence, evaluation is just opinion. AQA requires informed judgements backed by specific examples from the dance to show understanding.

tests.name: Exam-Style Practice
tests.description: Short-answer practice on Dance Appreciation Skills

questions.question: Q: How do the three appreciation skills of describe, analyse and evaluate work together?
questions.correctAnswer: You first describe what you see, then analyse how and why it works, and finally evaluate how effective it is — each skill builds on the previous one.

questions.question: Q: Why is using subject-specific terminology important in dance appreciation?
questions.correctAnswer: Accurate terminology shows precise understanding and communicates ideas clearly; vague language loses marks in the AQA written exam.
